stem: A 60-year-old man is seen 3 months after an anterior myocardial infarction. He takes his secondary-prevention drugs, has finished cardiac rehabilitation and has returned to work. His pulse is 64/min and his blood pressure is 128/78 mm Hg.
oneliner: 60M + anterior MI 3 months ago + doing well → which later sequela lowers survival?
ask: If it develops, which sequela of his infarction is most strongly linked to decreased survival?

whyNot.A: A lifelong trait, not a post-infarct event, and not shown to cut survival
whyNot.B: Common after MI and distressing, but **not an independent predictor of death**
whyNot.C: Platelets are not lowered after infarction; **reactivity rises** if anything
whyNot.E: Catecholamines are **raised**, not lowered, after infarction

why: Depression is **common after MI** (about 1 in 5 patients) and independently predicts **higher cardiac and all-cause mortality**. It lowers adherence to drugs and rehabilitation and is tied to higher sympathetic tone and platelet reactivity, so it should be **screened for and treated**.
chain: Poor adherence, higher sympathetic tone, more platelet activation
Higher risk of recurrent events and death

idea.rule: After MI, look for depression: it is common and carries its own mortality risk.
also: Depression also worsens outcomes in heart failure and stroke
Screen routinely after infarction (for example with PHQ-9)
Sertraline is a safe antidepressant after MI
Sexual dysfunction after MI needs counselling but is not a survival marker

stem: A 13-year-old girl has fever and swollen knees, then ankles, with pain that moves from joint to joint. She had a severe sore throat 3 weeks ago. Her antistreptolysin O titer is high. She is treated for the acute illness and then started on monthly penicillin injections that will continue for years.
oneliner: 13F + sore throat 3 wk ago + migratory joint pain + high ASO + monthly penicillin for years → what is prevented?
ask: This prophylaxis is aimed mainly at preventing which long-term sequela?

whyNot.A: Resolves on its own **without joint damage**; it is not the lasting harm
whyNot.B: A late neurologic feature that **also resolves** completely
whyNot.C: A histologic finding in the acute carditis, not a long-term complication
whyNot.D: An acute feature that heals; it does not leave a chronic lesion

why: Joint and neurologic features of acute rheumatic fever settle completely, but **valvulitis scars the mitral valve**. Repeated attacks keep reigniting it, so **secondary penicillin prophylaxis** prevents the **fibrotic mitral stenosis** that appears years later.
chain: Anti-M protein antibodies cross-react with heart

idea.rule: In rheumatic fever only the carditis causes permanent damage, and the mitral valve is hit most often.
also: Sydenham chorea resolves over weeks to months
Aortic valve is the second most involved
Aschoff bodies mark acute rheumatic carditis
